Elements of 99.9% purity or higher were weighed out, vacuum induction melted (VIM) and poured into a steel mold to produce 10 mm diameter cylindrical bars.

All samples were encapsulated in Ar-backfilled quartz ampoules and subsequently underwent the same homogenisation treatment at 1250 °C (above the γʹ solvus temperature) for 22 hours to reduce casting segregation and dissolve any primary γʹ.
This was followed by an aging treatment at 760 °C for 16 hours. The alloys were air cooled following both homogenisation and ageing heat treatments.

other.machine: 100 kN Mayes servohydraulic frame with Instron 8800 controller

evidence.quote: compression testing was carried out at room temperature using a low cycle fatigue machine comprising a 100 kN Mayes servohydraulic frame with an Instron 8800 controller.

evidence.quote: In all alloys, the tertiary γʹ were spherical and showed no sign of precipitate splitting.

In comparison with the secondary γʹ, the tertiary γʹ have higher Al contents and lower Ti contents. Notably, unexpectedly high contents of the γ-partitioning elements (Cr and Mo) were measured in the tertiary γʹ phase

property_observations.property: solid solution strengthening in γ matrix

evidence.quote: The effect of solid solution strengthening in the γ matrix phase was significant, giving up to ~300 MPa additional strength.
The magnitude of the total solid solution strengthening in the γ and tertiary γʹ phases increased with nominal Mo content across the alloy series
The largest strengthening effect is shown to arise through precipitation strengthening, for which the presence of Mo in these alloys is significant.
